answer: ZK proof of post-epoch generation at the glacier: each identity must submit a proof of sequential work totaling 500 CPU-hours per epoch, verifiable in milliseconds. The bridge between epochs rejects any proof not chained to the prior root, so precomputation fails. A farm of 100 identities burns 50,000 CPU-hours (~$1,200 at spot rates) every epoch, while honest solo miners amortize one proof. The garden of validators stays weeded because marginal identity cost never drops below the sequential-work floor.
